request.what: Withdraw treasury funds for Pallas by TxPipe: Maintaining Cardano's Core Rust Libraries, Year 2.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 540,750 ADA, consisting of 525,000 ADA for Pallas maintenance and enhancement plus a 15,750 ADA Intersect budget administration fee.
The motivation describes the underlying maintainer grant as 420,000 ADA plus a 105,000 ADA contingency reserve for a part-time Pallas maintainer over 12 months at an annual rate of $105,000 USD.

Pallas is described as a collection of Rust crates re-implementing core Ouroboros and Cardano primitives including CBOR encoding, cryptographic operations, mini-protocol networking, ledger traversal, transaction building, and address handling.
The proposal states that Pallas is used by projects including Aiken, Dolos, Lucid, Oura, Mithril, Amaru, UTxO-RPC, and others as shared infrastructure.
The proposal reports Pallas metrics of over 649 pull requests, 199 stars, 91 forks, 60 contributors, and 214,446 crates.io downloads, with links to GitHub and crates.io.

The stated maintenance scope covers dependency updates, protocol compatibility, performance improvements, bug fixing, documentation, issue triage, contribution review, ecosystem-feedback enhancements, public communication, and AI-friendly documentation and integration resources.

The proposal states it achieved the required 67% support threshold in the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and references voting, documentation, final audited results, and audit materials.
The proposal states that the withdrawal does not, at submission time alone or in aggregate, breach the applicable 350M ADA Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713.

The proposal states that Intersect will administer funds through Sundae Labs treasury management smart contracts with specified TRSC and PSSC addresses, role-based authorization thresholds, external oversight entities, and a public dashboard for auditability.

The proposal states TxPipe has received funding through 30 Project Catalyst proposals across Funds 9 through 14, with 26 successfully delivered and 4 under development and on schedule, plus prior Intersect maintenance funding for Pallas, Dolos, and UTxO RPC being delivered on schedule.

summary: The document requests 540,750 ADA for a 12-month continuation of Pallas maintenance by TxPipe, with stated public infrastructure benefits, adoption metrics, Intersect budget-process approval, NCL compliance, and smart-contract-based oversight, while some cost conversion and delivery-history claims are asserted rather than fully evidenced in the document.
